title: Azure File Share from C#
description: Mount Azure File shares and exchange files between ASP.NET Core and external systems.

data.text: Azure File Storage offers SMB-based file shares in the cloud. It is useful when an ASP.NET Core app needs to share files with on-premises systems, legacy tools, or containers.

items: Shared configuration or reference data accessed by multiple apps
Legacy integrations that require a mounted drive
Lift-and-shift scenarios where an app expects local filesystem paths

data.title: Blob vs File
data.text: For most new cloud-native ASP.NET Core apps, prefer Blob Storage. Use File Storage only when you need SMB semantics or existing file-share integration.

data.title: Create a file share with Azure CLI
data.content: Create a share inside an existing storage account.
data.code:
az storage share-account create \
  --account-name demostorageaccount \
  --name app-files \
  --resource-group azure-for-aspnet-rg

data.text: Upload and Download Files from C#

data.title: Upload and download with ShareFileClient
data.content: Use the `Azure.Storage.Files.Shares` package for file-share operations.

data.title: Export a CSV report to a file share
data.description: Generate a simple CSV report in ASP.NET Core and save it to Azure File Storage.
steps: Generate a CSV string from sample data
Upload it to the `exports` directory in the file share
Return the file name and share path to the caller
data.expectedOutcome: The file appears in the Azure file share and can be downloaded or mounted.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use Azure File Storage when you need SMB-compatible shared drives
Blob Storage is better for most cloud-native file scenarios
File shares are organized into directories and files
Use `ShareFileClient` for upload and download from C#
data.takeaway: File Storage bridges cloud and on-premises file workflows, while Blob Storage should be your default for web apps.
